text:
Alex: Heads up — nightly perf dashboard just alerted, 95th latency for small-seq workloads jumped ~2.1x around 23:10 UTC. :eyes:
ci-bot: Nightly perf check: metric=llm_infer.latency_p95, baseline=120ms, current=255ms, delta=+112.5%, alert_id=perf-nt-2934
Priya: ugh. did something land during the 22:00 deploy window?
Sam: yep, merged adaptive-scheduler v3.2.1 (PR #2147) at 22:07. it tweaks batcher window and kernel selection thresholds.
Jordan: interesting — I changed the kernel fallback ordering in that PR to prefer stream_kernel for short sequences. maybe the selection heuristic misfires under prefix cache pressure.
Maya: checking KV metrics now — kv.cache_hit_rate_smallseq dropped from 0.92 -> 0.67 ~22:15. that matches the latency spike.
Alex: can we get a quick flamegraph/pprof for an affected host? Maya — any profiling artifacts?
Maya: uploading a pprof from node infer-03 to cidrive: https://internal.ci/redwood/pprof/2934556789/infer-03.pprof 
Maya: top shows hot path: batcher::evaluate_heuristic -> kernel_selector::score_stream_kernel -> kv::ensure_prefix_loaded
Priya: so selection is choosing stream_kernel earlier which triggers cold KV loads more often?
Sam: that tracks. stream_kernel reduces per-token compute but expects KV already warm. if we pick it while KV is cold, latency explodes.
Jordan: I remember adding an epsilon tweak to bias towards stream_kernel when seq_len < 48. maybe the epsilon is too aggressive for noisy prefix distributions at night.
Alex: do we have a quick repro in CI? Nightly perf job failed; logs attached: https://internal.ci/redwood/nightly/2934556789/logs
ci-bot: job=nightly-perf-2934, status=FAILED, failed_tests=[p95_small_seq_latency], artifact=https://internal.ci/artifacts/nightly-2934.tgz
Sam: I'll run a bisect on the branch that produced the canary. starting with commits between c7d9a6 (pre) and f2b1c3 (post).
Priya: meanwhile, hold the rollout — set canary=0 for that release, please. we don't want more users hitting it.
Sam: done. @deploy-bot set rollout=0 for release/adaptive-scheduler/3.2.1 :white_check_mark:
Maya: quick experiment: reverted the kernel bias locally by setting KERNEL_BIAS=0.0 and replayed 2000 requests from the midnight trace — p95 dropped back to 128ms.
Jordan: good signal. if bisect points at the epsilon commit, we should either relax it or gate by kv.hot_ratio > 0.8.
Alex: agree. Sam — status of bisect?
Sam: bisect halfway: commit 3f4e2b (kernel-ordering change) as first suspect. running targeted nightly on a canary pool with artificial prefix churn. will update in ~20m.
Priya: add a check in the selection code to prefer kernel=A when kv.miss_rate > 0.1, as a temporary safety. can we patch and run quick smoke?
Jordan: I can put a fast patch in master: guard + metric check, no rebuild required (runtime flag). pushing now.
Jordan: pushed flag guard: runtime flag kernel.selection_avoid_stream_on_kv_miss=true (rollout via config service).
Maya: toggled the flag in canary; rerunning the failing replay — p95 now 126ms. KV miss rate still high but we avoid stream kernel.
Sam: bisect now shows the performance regression correlates with commit 3f4e2b and the epsilon tweak in commit bd12ac. both together amplified the KV coldstart effect.
Alex: plan: revert bd12ac (epsilon tweak) in a follow-up and keep the runtime guard until we have better telemetry. also add a metric-based test in nightly to catch this pattern.
Priya: also add an eval that replays traces with varying prefix churn to keep selection heuristics honest.
Sam: opening revert PR now and will request urgent review. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/PR/2201
Maya: after revert + guard, I'm seeing nightly metrics return to baseline for 3 consecutive runs. marked as investig-closed in the dashboard.
Alex: nice triage. postmortem follow-ups: (1) add unit test + replay harness, (2) add KV-aware gating to kernel selector, (3) add CI perf guard for p95_small_seq.
Priya: noted. thanks everyone for the fast loop. :tada:
